1.why: Every MFA endpoint resolves the account solely from the server-side session map via auth() (checking s.userId === account.id), and suppliedIdentifier() rejects any client-supplied user/account identifier in the query string or JSON body with 403.

2.why: The statement is false: the OTP is verified against the per-account pending secret decrypted server-side (and recovery codes are matched against that account's hashes), so a code cannot be used for a different account — the single-account model provides no cross-user code path at all.

3.why: The statement is true: /api/mfa/verify sets account.enabled = true but never rotates the cookie or deletes entries from the sessions map, so any session existing before MFA enrolment continues to work (rotation only happens at /api/login).

4.why: The pending TOTP seed and account.secret are stored only as AES-GCM ciphertext, and each recovery code is stored as a SHA-256 hash plus an AES-GCM encrypted copy — no plaintext at rest (though the reversible copy allows retrieval via /api/mfa/recovery).

5.why: Session tokens, CSRF tokens, CSP nonces, the Base32 TOTP seed, AES key/IVs and recovery codes are all derived from crypto.getRandomValues().

6.why: The session cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict and no localStorage/sessionStorage is used (CSRF token and logs live only in JS memory), although the provisioning secret, test OTP and recovery codes are rendered into the DOM and console.

7.why: Server-side validation includes emailOK/phoneOK regexes, strict /^\d{6}$/ for OTP, a strict recovery-code pattern, content-type and 4 KB length checks, and rejection of unexpected identifier keys; there is no SQL layer to inject into.

8.why: All dynamic values inserted via innerHTML pass through esc() (textContent→innerHTML encoding) as element text, and a per-response nonce CSP with script-src 'self' 'nonce-…' blocks injected inline script.

9.why: There are no server-issued redirects and client navigation only uses location.hash with a fixed internal set of view names, so no open-redirect path exists — but no explicit allow-list mechanism is implemented either.

10.why: headers() sets a nonce-based CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', HSTS with includeSubDomains, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy on every response.

11.why: The bank_session cookie is issued as `Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` on login and cleared with the same attributes on logout.

12.why: Server errors are generic ("Unable to complete this request.") with no stack traces or secrets in URLs, but the client explicitly console.log()s and renders into a visible Logs panel the provisioning secret, the test OTP, and all recovery codes.

13.why: The pending enrolment has a 5-minute expiry and a used flag set on successful verification, and recovery codes are marked used once redeemed; however a TOTP value remains replayable within its 30–60 s window before success since no per-step consumption is recorded.

14.why: Both OTP verification and recovery redemption lock out for 10 minutes after 5 failures, but the failure counter is reset to 0 when the lock is applied and /api/login itself has only a timing floor with no attempt throttling.

15.why: Login deletes any prior session token and issues a fresh one, auth() enforces a 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeout, and /api/logout removes the session from the map and clears the cookie.
